provenance.note: Standard relations of introductory physics, written for this pack; no source text is reproduced.

relations.name: Speed after a displacement under constant acceleration
Displacement from the mean of initial and final velocity
Weight in a uniform gravitational field

default.assumption: standard gravity g = 9.80665 m/s^2 near Earth's surface

relations.name: Net force with an opposing friction force
assumptions: applied force and friction act along the same line, in opposite directions

relations.name: Sliding friction
assumptions: the surfaces slide over each other

relations.name: Normal force on a level surface
Linear momentum
assumptions: speeds far below the speed of light

relations.name: Work by a constant force

default.assumption: the force acts along the displacement

fails_when: the force is friction and no angle is stated: friction opposes the motion (180 degrees), which must be said, not assumed

relations.name: Translational kinetic energy
assumptions: speeds far below the speed of light

relations.name: Gravitational potential energy near the surface

default.assumption: standard gravity g = 9.80665 m/s^2 near Earth's surface

assumptions: zero of potential energy at h = 0

relations.name: Force of a linear spring
assumptions: linear elastic spring within its elastic limit

relations.name: Energy stored in a linear spring
assumptions: linear elastic spring within its elastic limit

relations.name: Power of a force on a moving body
Speed on a circle from angular speed
Pressure of a force on an area
assumptions: force spread evenly and normal to the surface

relations.name: Pressure of a column of fluid

default.assumption: standard gravity g = 9.80665 m/s^2 near Earth's surface

assumptions: fluid at rest with uniform density
pressure measured relative to the surface

relations.name: Voltage across an ohmic resistance
assumptions: ohmic element at a fixed temperature

relations.name: Charge carried by a steady current
Speed of a periodic wave
assumptions: periodic wave in a uniform medium

relations.name: Heat for a temperature change
assumptions: specific heat constant over the range

relations.name: Maximum height of a vertical throw

h.desc: maximum height above the launch point

default.assumption: standard gravity g = 9.80665 m/s^2 near Earth's surface

relations.frame: vertical axis through the launch point
conventions: speeds and heights are magnitudes; upward is the direction of launch
h is the height of the highest point only; it is not the displacement at any other moment
applies_when: the launch is vertical
the height is measured from the launch point
fails_when: the launch is at an angle

relations.name: Time to the top of a vertical throw

t.desc: time from launch to the highest point

default.assumption: standard gravity g = 9.80665 m/s^2 near Earth's surface

relations.frame: vertical axis through the launch point
conventions: the launch speed is a magnitude
applies_when: the launch is vertical
fails_when: the time asked for is the whole flight

relations.name: Normal force on an incline

default.assumption: standard gravity g = 9.80665 m/s^2 near Earth's surface

theta.desc: angle of the incline to the horizontal

assumptions: no acceleration perpendicular to the incline
no other force with a component normal to the surface
relations.frame: axes along and normal to the incline
conventions: the angle is measured from the horizontal
applies_when: the body rests or slides on a straight incline
fails_when: another force pushes into or pulls away from the surface

relations.name: Component of the weight along an incline

F.desc: component of the weight along the incline

default.assumption: standard gravity g = 9.80665 m/s^2 near Earth's surface

theta.desc: angle of the incline to the horizontal

relations.frame: axes along and normal to the incline
conventions: the angle is measured from the horizontal
the component points down the incline; its magnitude is given
applies_when: a body is on a straight incline

relations.name: Acceleration down a frictionless incline

default.assumption: standard gravity g = 9.80665 m/s^2 near Earth's surface

theta.desc: angle of the incline to the horizontal

assumptions: the only forces are gravity and the normal force
relations.frame: axis along the incline, positive downhill
conventions: the acceleration is the magnitude down the incline
applies_when: the surface is stated to be frictionless
fails_when: another force acts along the incline
any other force is stated (a push, a pull, a rope)

relations.name: Speed of a body launched by a spring

x.desc: compression of the spring before release

v.desc: speed when the spring has returned to its natural length

assumptions: all the energy stored in the spring becomes kinetic energy of the body
relations.frame: motion along the axis of the spring on a level surface
applies_when: the body starts at rest against the compressed spring and is released
the surface is frictionless and level
fails_when: the body is still attached and the spring is not at its natural length
the motion is vertical or on a slope

relations.name: Work-energy theorem

W.desc: net work done on the body, equal to its change in kinetic energy

assumptions: W is the work of ALL forces on the body
speeds far below the speed of light
conventions: speeds are magnitudes; the net work is negative when the body slows
applies_when: the work stated is the net (total) work on the body
fails_when: only the work of one of several forces is known

relations.name: Tension in a rope holding a hanging body

default.assumption: standard gravity g = 9.80665 m/s^2 near Earth's surface

assumptions: one vertical rope carries the whole weight
applies_when: the body hangs at rest or moves at constant velocity from a single vertical rope
fails_when: several ropes or ropes at an angle share the load

relations.name: Average net force from a change of momentum

t.desc: time over which the momentum changes

assumptions: F is the net force averaged over the interval
relations.frame: a line, with one direction taken as positive
conventions: momenta carry signs; a negative force opposes the positive direction
applies_when: the momentum before and after is known
fails_when: the force asked for is one of several forces

relations.name: Speed after falling from rest

default.assumption: standard gravity g = 9.80665 m/s^2 near Earth's surface

applies_when: the body starts from rest and falls freely

relations.name: Force on a charge in an electric field

Ef.desc: electric field strength at the charge

applies_when: a charge sits in a known electric field
fails_when: the charge's own field is asked for
conventions: magnitudes; the direction follows the sign of the charge

relations.name: Electric field of a point charge

default.assumption: Coulomb's constant k = 8.99e9 N*m^2/C^2 (charges in vacuum or air)

applies_when: outside a point or spherical charge
fails_when: inside a conductor or a dielectric

relations.name: Electric potential of a point charge

default.assumption: Coulomb's constant k = 8.99e9 N*m^2/C^2 (charges in vacuum or air)

applies_when: outside a point or spherical charge
fails_when: the reference point is not at infinity
conventions: potential relative to infinity; magnitudes of charge

relations.name: Potential difference in a uniform field
applies_when: between parallel plates far from their edges

relations.name: Charge on a capacitor
applies_when: a charged capacitor

relations.name: Energy stored in a capacitor
applies_when: a charged capacitor
fails_when: the capacitor leaks or breaks down
conventions: energy stored in the field between the plates

relations.name: Capacitance of parallel plates

default.assumption: the permittivity of free space e0 = 8.854e-12 C^2/(N*m^2) (vacuum or air between the plates)

assumptions: plates much wider than their separation
vacuum or air between the plates
applies_when: parallel plates with air or vacuum between them
fails_when: the plates are small compared with their separation

relations.name: Power from current and resistance
applies_when: a resistor carries a steady current

relations.name: Power from voltage and resistance
applies_when: a resistor has a steady voltage across it

relations.name: Resistance of a uniform wire
applies_when: an ohmic conductor of uniform cross-section

relations.name: Magnetic force on a moving charge
relations.frame: angle between the velocity and the field
applies_when: a charge moving in a magnetic field
conventions: magnitudes; the direction follows the right-hand rule

relations.name: Magnetic force on a current-carrying wire

L.desc: length of wire in the field

theta.desc: angle between the wire and the field

applies_when: a straight wire in a uniform magnetic field
fails_when: the field varies along the wire

relations.name: Magnetic field of a long straight wire

default.assumption: the permeability of free space mu0 = 1.2566e-6 T*m/A (vacuum or air)

applies_when: near a long straight wire, far from its ends
fails_when: near the ends of a short wire

relations.name: Magnetic field inside a long solenoid

default.assumption: the permeability of free space mu0 = 1.2566e-6 T*m/A (vacuum or air)

relations.frame: inside the solenoid, far from its ends
applies_when: inside a long solenoid

relations.name: Gravitational acceleration at a distance from a mass

M.desc: mass of the planet or star

default.assumption: the gravitational constant G = 6.674e-11 N*m^2/kg^2

applies_when: at or above the surface of a planet or star

relations.name: Speed in a circular orbit

default.assumption: the gravitational constant G = 6.674e-11 N*m^2/kg^2

assumptions: the orbiting body much lighter than the central one
applies_when: a satellite in a circular orbit

relations.name: Period of a circular orbit

default.assumption: the gravitational constant G = 6.674e-11 N*m^2/kg^2

assumptions: the orbiting body much lighter than the central one
applies_when: a satellite in a circular orbit

relations.name: Ideal gas law

default.assumption: the gas constant R = 8.314 J/(mol*K)

applies_when: a dilute gas far from condensation

relations.name: Heat to melt or freeze
assumptions: no temperature change during the phase change
applies_when: melting or freezing at the melting point

relations.name: Heat to boil or condense
assumptions: no temperature change during the phase change
applies_when: boiling or condensing at the boiling point

relations.name: Linear thermal expansion
assumptions: the coefficient constant over the range
applies_when: solids over moderate temperature ranges
conventions: a rise in temperature lengthens the object

relations.name: Thin lens equation
applies_when: a thin lens
conventions: real images positive, virtual negative; converging f > 0

relations.name: Energy of a photon

default.assumption: Planck's constant h = 6.626e-34 J*s

applies_when: light or other electromagnetic radiation
fails_when: a classical wave energy is asked for

relations.name: Photon energy from wavelength

default.assumption: Planck's constant h = 6.626e-34 J*s
the speed of light in vacuum c = 2.998e8 m/s

applies_when: light in vacuum or air
fails_when: the wavelength is measured in a medium

relations.name: Momentum of a photon

default.assumption: Planck's constant h = 6.626e-34 J*s

applies_when: light
fails_when: massive particles (use the de Broglie relation)

relations.name: De Broglie wavelength

default.assumption: Planck's constant h = 6.626e-34 J*s

applies_when: electrons, protons, neutrons and other particles

relations.name: Rest energy

default.assumption: the speed of light in vacuum c = 2.998e8 m/s

assumptions: energy of the mass at rest
applies_when: mass converted entirely into energy, or the rest energy of a body
fails_when: the kinetic energy is also wanted

relations.name: Period of a simple pendulum

default.assumption: standard gravity g = 9.80665 m/s^2 near Earth's surface

assumptions: a point mass on a light string
applies_when: small-angle swings
conventions: one full swing back and forth

relations.name: Period of a mass on a spring
applies_when: a mass oscillating on an ideal spring

relations.name: Torque of a force

r.desc: distance from the pivot to the point of application

applies_when: a force applied at a distance from a pivot

relations.name: Rotational kinetic energy
assumptions: a rigid body rotating about a fixed axis
applies_when: a rotating rigid body

relations.name: Angular momentum of a rotating body
assumptions: a rigid body rotating about a fixed axis
applies_when: a rotating rigid body

relations.name: Tangential acceleration of a point on a rotating body
assumptions: a rigid body about a fixed axis
applies_when: a point on a rotating rigid body

relations.name: Centripetal acceleration from angular velocity
applies_when: motion on a circle at constant angular velocity

relations.name: Angular momentum of a point mass on a circle
assumptions: a point mass moving perpendicular to the radius
applies_when: a small body moving on a circle

relations.name: Absolute pressure at a depth in a fluid

default.assumption: standard gravity g = 9.80665 m/s^2 near Earth's surface

relations.frame: depth measured down from the surface
applies_when: a liquid at rest
fails_when: the fluid is accelerating or compressible over the depth

relations.name: Flow rate as volume per time
applies_when: a fluid flows through a pipe or opening
fails_when: the flow is unsteady and an instantaneous rate is asked

relations.name: Flow rate through a cross section
assumptions: the average speed over the cross section
applies_when: a fluid flows through a pipe
fails_when: the flow is not along the pipe

relations.name: Thermal expansion of volume
applies_when: solids and liquids over moderate temperature changes
fails_when: phase changes or large temperature ranges

relations.name: Efficiency of a heat engine

Qh.desc: heat taken in from the hot reservoir

assumptions: efficiency as a fraction, not a percentage
applies_when: a heat engine over whole cycles

relations.name: Carnot (maximum) efficiency
assumptions: a reversible engine between two reservoirs
applies_when: an ideal engine between two reservoirs
fails_when: temperatures in degrees Celsius used as absolute

relations.name: Maximum speed of a mass on a spring
applies_when: a mass oscillating on a spring

relations.name: Intensity as power per area

A.desc: area perpendicular to the flow of energy

assumptions: power spread uniformly over the area
applies_when: waves or radiation falling on a surface

relations.name: Wavelength of light in a medium
assumptions: the frequency is unchanged across the boundary
applies_when: light entering a transparent medium

relations.name: Index of refraction

default.assumption: the speed of light in vacuum c = 2.998e8 m/s

v.desc: speed of light in the medium

applies_when: transparent materials

relations.name: Focal length of a spherical mirror
applies_when: spherical mirrors with small apertures

relations.name: Rms voltage of a sinusoidal supply
applies_when: sinusoidal AC

relations.name: Rms current of a sinusoidal supply
applies_when: sinusoidal AC

relations.name: Magnetic field at the centre of a circular loop

default.assumption: the permeability of free space mu0 = 1.2566e-6 T*m/A (vacuum or air)

applies_when: the centre of a circular current loop

relations.name: Time constant of an RL circuit
applies_when: an RL circuit switched on or off

relations.name: Reactance of an inductor
applies_when: an inductor in an AC circuit

relations.name: Reactance of a capacitor
applies_when: a capacitor in an AC circuit

relations.name: Resonant frequency of an LC circuit
applies_when: LC and series RLC circuits

relations.name: Angular velocity under constant angular acceleration
applies_when: a body spins up or down about a fixed axis

relations.name: Angular velocity and angle turned under constant angular acceleration
applies_when: a body spins up or down about a fixed axis

relations.name: Energy balance of a cyclic heat engine

Qh.desc: heat in from the hot reservoir

Qc.desc: heat out to the cold reservoir

assumptions: a cyclic engine (no net change in internal energy)
applies_when: a heat engine over whole cycles

relations.name: Coefficient of performance of a refrigerator

Qc.desc: heat removed from the cold space

applies_when: refrigerators and air conditioners
fails_when: a heat pump (heat delivered is the benefit)

relations.name: Coefficient of performance of a heat pump

Qh.desc: heat delivered to the warm space

applies_when: heat pumps heating a building

relations.name: Radius of a charged particle's circle in a magnetic field

theta.desc: angle between the velocity and the field

assumptions: the path is the circle traced by the perpendicular velocity component
applies_when: a charged particle in a uniform magnetic field
fails_when: relativistic speeds or a velocity component along the field

relations.name: Time constant of an RC circuit
applies_when: an RC circuit charging or discharging

relations.name: Voltage of a discharging capacitor

V.desc: voltage across the capacitor at time t

applies_when: a charged capacitor discharging through a resistor

relations.name: Voltage of a charging capacitor

V.desc: voltage across the capacitor at time t

assumptions: the capacitor is uncharged at t = 0
applies_when: an uncharged capacitor charged through a resistor by a constant emf

relations.name: Thermal expansion of an area
assumptions: the coefficient constant over the range
applies_when: flat solids over moderate temperature ranges
conventions: a rise in temperature enlarges the area

relations.name: Emf of a rod moving through a magnetic field
assumptions: B, the rod and its velocity mutually perpendicular
applies_when: a straight rod moving through a uniform magnetic field

relations.name: Current dying away in an RL circuit

t.desc: time since the circuit was switched off

assumptions: the source is removed at t = 0
applies_when: an RL circuit after the source is switched off
